Location: Richmond, BC

Work Arrangement: Hybrid, 4 days on site (Monday to Thursday)

Job Summary

Semtech is building the next generation of AI-powered commercial workflows across its global sales organization. This 8-month co-op is a hands-on, production-oriented role embedded within Sales Operations. You will work directly with the Senior Director of Global Sales Operations to design, test, and document AI-enabled workflows that improve efficiency, consistency, and insight across real sales processes. This is not a research role — your work will be used by sellers, distributors, and sales leadership. The ideal candidate is curious, operationally minded, and has a genuine interest in applying AI to solve business problems. 

This role is best suited for students who enjoy figuring out how things work and making them work better. You don’t need to be a software engineer — but you do need to be comfortable with data, curious about AI, and motivated by operational impact. If you’ve ever built a workflow to automate something in your own life, used AI tools to solve a real problem, or found yourself thinking ‘there has to be a better way to do this’ — this is for you. 

Responsibilities

AI Workflow Development & Testing 




-  Research, design, and build AI-enabled workflow automations targeting repeatable sales operations tasks (e.g., account research, CRM data enrichment, meeting prep, follow-up summaries)  
-  Test and validate workflows across edge cases to ensure accuracy, reliability, and repeatability before deployment  
-  Configure AI-assisted summarization, data processing, and exception-based logic steps within approved operational frameworks  
-  Support prompt engineering and iteration for tools including Claude, Microsoft Copilot, and Vinton AI  
-  Document automation logic, inputs, outputs, and governance notes so solutions can be maintained and reused  

 Sales Process & Data Analysis 




-  Map existing sales workflows to identify friction points, manual steps, and automation candidates  
-  Analyze operational and CRM data to surface trends, gaps, and opportunities for AI-assisted improvement  
-  Assist in building dashboards and reports to track AI tool adoption, usage patterns, and productivity impact  
-  Support data preparation, cleaning, and validation to ensure high-quality inputs for AI workflows  

 Collaboration & Communication 




-  Work cross-functionally with Sales Enablement, Salesforce Admins, and commercial team members to gather requirements and validate solutions  
-  Present findings, workflow designs, and test results to the Sales Operations and AI Ambassador teams and relevant stakeholders  
-  Contribute to documentation, knowledge base articles, and user guides for deployed AI workflows  
-  Participate in the AI Ambassador program and support broader AI adoption initiatives across the commercial team  

What You’ll Gain




-  Direct exposure to how AI is applied within a real enterprise sales environment — not academic simulations  
-  Hands-on experience with leading AI tools: Claude, Microsoft Copilot, Vinton AI, and Salesforce-integrated AI agents  
-  Practical skills in workflow design, operational analytics, and stakeholder communication  
-  Experience that translates directly into careers in Sales Ops, Revenue Ops, AI Strategy, or Digital Transformation  
-  Mentorship from a Sales Operations Leader with active responsibility for AI adoption across a global commercial team  

Minimum Qualifications




-  Currently enrolled in a post-secondary program in Business, Business Analytics, Information Systems, Computer Science, or a related field  
-  Demonstrated interest in AI tools and workflow automation — through coursework, personal projects, or hands-on experimentation  
-  Basic understanding of sales processes and commercial operations (e.g., lead management, pipeline, CRM usage)  
-  Strong analytical thinking with the ability to break down operational problems and propose structured solutions  
-  Proficiency in Microsoft 365 (Excel, SharePoint, Teams); comfort working in data-rich environments  
-  Clear written and verbal communication skills; able to document technical logic for non-technical audiences  
-  Ability to work independently with minimal direction and navigate ambiguity  

Desired Qualifications




-  Hands-on experience with generative AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, or equivalent) in an applied or academic context  
-  Programming experience in Python, particularly for data manipulation, automation scripting, or API interaction  
-  Familiarity with Salesforce CRM — even basic navigation or coursework (Trailhead counts)  
-  Experience with data visualization tools such as Power BI or Tableau  
-  Exposure to prompt engineering, LLM-based workflows, or no-code/low-code automation platforms (Zapier, Power Automate, n8n, or similar)  
-  Knowledge of SQL or experience querying structured datasets  
-  Prior co-op or internship experience in a business operations, analytics, or technology role

role: Software Engineering Intern - Summer 2027 - Native SDK & Mobile Platforms
jd:
About Niantic Spatial

AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time.

That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are.

In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right.

Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us.



About the Role

This internship sits at the intersection of systems engineering, mobile application development, and applied research. You'll work directly with platform, research, and application engineers to turn new capabilities in spatial computing, localization, and computer vision into polished experiences for developers and end users — from shared C++ runtime code and native Swift/Kotlin SDKs to production-quality iOS and Android applications.

Depending on your interests and the projects underway, you may work deeper in the platform stack, closer to the application layer, or across both. You'll also use AI-assisted workflows to move quickly across platforms while maintaining high standards for native quality and user experience.



What You'll Do

 - Native & Cross-Platform Development — Build features in Swift, Kotlin, and C++, ranging from user-facing mobile experiences to the runtime and SDK capabilities that power them.

 - Research-to-Product Engineering — Help turn research prototypes in spatial computing, localization, and computer vision into production-quality SDK features and intuitive mobile application experiences.

 - Mobile Application Development — Build and refine native iOS and Android experiences that exercise new platform capabilities, solve real user problems, and help define how our technology should work in practice.

 - AI-Assisted Engineering — Use AI-assisted development workflows to implement, adapt, and maintain functionality across multiple native platforms without sacrificing platform-specific quality.

 - Cross-Boundary Debugging — Debug problems across the full stack, from shared C++ runtime behavior and native bindings through application logic, UI, device sensors, and real-world usage.

 - Quality, Performance & Tooling — Write automated tests, improve build and release tooling, investigate performance, and validate new capabilities through on-device testing and sensor playback.

 - Product & API Collaboration — Work with research, platform, design, and application engineers to shape APIs and user experiences that are stable, ergonomic, and useful across a growing range of devices and use cases.



What You'll Bring

 - Currently pursuing a BS or MS in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related technical field.

 - Demonstrated experience building software in C++, Swift, Kotlin, or another native or systems language through coursework, personal projects, research, or prior internships.

 - Strong interest in native mobile development, SDKs, libraries, and developer-facing platforms with an appreciation for performance, API design, and platform-specific behavior.

 - Ability to independently investigate unfamiliar systems, debug across platform boundaries, and turn ambiguous technical problems into working, maintainable solutions.

 - Strong engineering instincts around testing, code quality, API ergonomics, and maintainability with the judgment to balance shared abstractions against platform-native conventions.

 - Comfort using AI-assisted development tools to increase engineering velocity across iOS, Android, and shared C++ code.

 - Available for 4 days per week in our San Francisco office for the full 12-week internship.



Nice to Have

 - Hands-on experience with iOS (Xcode, Instruments) or Android (Android Studio, Android NDK) development environments.

 - Familiarity with spatial computing, augmented reality, computer vision, or localization (SLAM, VPS).

 - Experience with cross-platform build systems such as CMake or Bazel.

 - Prior exposure to SDK or library development, open-source contributions, or developer-facing APIs.



Compensation & Benefits

The expected hourly rate for this internship is $48 – $70/hour, based on assessed skills, experience, and relevant coursework. Housing assistance and relocation support available for candidates outside the Bay Area — details provided during the offer process.



Location & Work Model

This internship is based in our San Francisco, CA office. We work in a high-collaboration environment and ask interns to be on-site a minimum of 4 days per week. To make that easy, we provide lunch every day and snacks are always stocked.



Inclusive Application

We know the strongest candidates don't always tick every box. If you're excited about this role and believe you could do it well, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't match every qualification listed — you may be exactly who we're looking for.



Equal Opportunity

Niantic Spatial is an equal opportunity employer. Individuals seeking employment at Niantic Spatial are considered without regard to race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, creed, age, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, breastfeeding or related medical conditions), marital status, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, or any other protected category under applicable laws. Niantic Spatial will also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in accordance with applicable laws. Please contact your recruiter if you want to request an accommodation for the job application or interview process.



Candidate Privacy

I understand that by submitting my job application, the information I provide as part of that application will be used in accordance with Niantic Spatial's Privacy Notice for Job Applicants and Candidates https://www.nianticspatial.com/applicant-privacy-notice.

Who we are

Aurora’s mission is to deliver the benefits of self-driving technology safely, quickly, and broadly.

The Aurora Driver https://aurora.tech will create a new era in mobility and logistics, one that will bring a safer, more efficient, and more accessible future to everyone.

At Aurora, you will tackle massively complex problems alongside other passionate, intelligent individuals, growing as an expert while expanding your knowledge. For the latest news from Aurora, visit aurora.tech http://aurora.tech or follow us on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/auroradriver.

 

What we are looking for

We're searching for Summer 2027 Core Autonomy Software Interns. You'll work on the low-level software that runs the Aurora Driver reliably in real time, onboard compute and robotics middleware, system software architecture, autonomy integration, and real-time routing/graph systems.

In this role you will

 - Write and integrate C++ software that runs onboard the Aurora Driver under real-time constraints

 - Work on system software architecture, middleware, or autonomy integration depending on team placement

 - Reason about latency, memory, and reliability tradeoffs rather than just passing unit tests

 - Use performance analysis and instrumentation tools to diagnose real system behavior

 - Partner with full-time engineers on production-quality code, not prototype-only work

Required qualifications

 - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, or a related field

 - Strong C++ and general systems-programming skills

 - Some real-time and/or embedded systems exposure

 - Working knowledge of graph algorithms and core data structures

 - Ability to reason about latency, memory, and reliability constraints

 - Experience targeting a Linux-like development environment

Desirable qualifications

 - Experience with Linux kernel internals and/or kernel driver development

 - Experience with performance analysis tools (e.g. eBPF-based tooling)

Compensation

The hourly pay rate for this internship in Mountain View is:

 - $52.00 per hour for interns pursuing a bachelor’s degree; and

 - $58.00 per hour for interns pursuing a master’s degree

The hourly pay rate for this internship in Pittsburgh is:

 - $47.00 per hour for interns pursuing a bachelor’s degree; and

 - $52.00 per hour for interns pursuing a master’s degree



Working at Aurora

At Aurora, we bring together extraordinarily talented and experienced people united by the strength of our values. We operate with integrity, set outrageous goals, and build a culture where we win together — all without any jerks.

We believe in-person work increases collaboration, empathy, and our ability to lead effectively. As a result, Aurorans are expected to work from the office at least 3 days per week, with some roles requiring more frequent in-office presence, up to 5 days per week, based on operational needs.

Our Careers page https://aurora.tech/careers provides insight into what it is like to work at Aurora, and you can find all the latest updates in our Newsroom https://aurora.tech/newsroom.



Our commitment to safety

At the core of everything we do is our commitment to safety. Building best-in-class self-driving technology will take time, and we believe that each employee at Aurora has a role in contributing to safety, every step of the way. Aurora expects commitment to our safety policies from every employee, and seeks candidates who take an active responsibility, can contribute to building an atmosphere of trust, and invest in the organization’s long-term success by prioritizing working safely, no matter what.



Our commitment to inclusion

Aurora considers candidates without regard to their race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, pregnancy status, parent or caregiver status, ancestry, political affiliation, veteran and/or military status, physical or mental disability, or any other status protected by federal or state law. Aurora considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law. We are also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at careersiteaccommodations@aurora.tech.





For California applicants, information collected and processed as part of your application and any job applications you choose to submit is subject to Aurora’s California Employment Privacy Policy.
